newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP not sure if official rate rise needed.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP not sure if official rate rise needed.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland's Deputy President Witold Kozinski said on Monday it was still not clear whether the central bank needed to raise official interest rates.
"There still are no clear (indications) for or against an possible decision about increasing interest rates," the Rzeczpospolita daily quoted Kozinski as saying.
Kozinski also said that according to preliminary NBP estimates broad money supply grew 5.2 percent, or 6.6 billion zlotys in December, after rising 1.4 percent in November.
The central bank is expected to officially release December broad money data later this week.

Kozinski said the central bank was still waiting to see whether its recent increase of market rates, from about 19.5 to 22 percent over the last month, would have the desired effect of curbing fast growing credit growth.
"It is almost certain that interest in consumer credit will drop, but it is not clear how firms will react (to the increase of market rates)," Kozinski said.
He said company debt accounted for 75 percent of all credit to the non-financial sector, which boomed by over 40 percent last year and was one of the main engines of the economy.

Kozinski said the large broad money increase in December was caused by both seasonal end-of-year outflows and by an increase of so-called float money, cash tied up in clearing operations as many Polish banks changed account numbers.
He said that the absence of such factors could cause broad money supply to decrease in nominal terms in January. @
Kozinski also reiterated the central bank's 1997 exchange rate policy, which envisages no real-term appreciation or significant weakening of the Polish zloty this year.

"The key of this year's exchange rate policy will be not to allow the zloty to appreciate in real terms on one side, and not to allow a significant devaluation on the other, which could increase inflation," Kozinski said.
